chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hakam ibn Maskin, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I borrow a loaf of bread from the neighbors, so we take a large one and give a small one, or we take a small one and give a large one?' He said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to borrow a large loaf of bread and return a small one to a neighbor?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permits borrowing bread from neighbors with the flexibility of returning either a larger or smaller loaf, reflecting the practical reality of small, consumable goods where exact equivalence is often difficult to maintain. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle of *ease* (taysir) in daily social transactions, prioritizing neighborly goodwill and the removal of hardship over rigid contractual precision for minor items.
